title: Additivity of complexity under the product of protocols
statement: Fix input types $X$, $Y$, a private-randomness type $\Omega_X$ for Alice and $\Omega_Y$ for Bob, and output types $\alpha_1$, $\alpha_2$. Let $p_1$ be a private-coin finite-message protocol producing an output in $\alpha_1$, and let $p_2$ be a deterministic finite-message protocol over $X$, $Y$ producing an output in $\alpha_2$. Form their product, the private-coin protocol that runs $p_1$ and then $p_2$ on the same inputs (with $p_2$ using no private randomness) and reports the pair of their outputs in $\alpha_1 \times \alpha_2$. Then the worst-case communication cost of this product equals the sum of the individual costs, that is, the complexity of the product is the complexity of $p_1$ plus the complexity of $p_2$.
hypotheses_covered: p1 is a private-coin finite-message protocol with output in α₁
p2 is a deterministic finite-message protocol with output in α₂
replaced:
The communication complexity of \texttt{prodDet}~$p_1$~$p_2$ equals the sum of both
complexities: $(\mathrm{prodDet}\;p_1\;p_2).\mathrm{complexity} = p_1.\mathrm{complexity} + p_2.\mathrm{complexity}$.
